instruction: Set the speaker volume to 90% for a loud but not maximum setting.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command:
pulseaudio --start
pactl list sinks | grep '^[[:space:]]Volume:' | head -n 1 | awk '{print $5}' | sed 's/%//g'

metadata.explanation: Task requires agent to set system volume to 90%. Evaluator uses pactl command to check volume percentage, expecting '90\n' output. Uses existing exact_match metric and vm_command_line getter - no custom functions needed.
metadata.verification: Verified that pactl command returns volume percentage as integer (0-100) followed by newline. Volume 90% produces output '90\n'.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly uses pactl command to extract current volume percentage from PulseAudio sinks
The command pipeline (pactl list sinks | grep | awk | sed) correctly parses volume output to extract percentage value
Metric exact_match appropriately checks if volume equals exactly 90%
Expected value '90\n' matches the actual output format of the command
Complete coverage: instruction requires setting volume to 90%, evaluator verifies volume is 90%
Command includes 'pulseaudio --start' to ensure PulseAudio is running before querying
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor consideration: Command uses 'head -n 1' which only checks the first sink - this assumes a single default sink system, which is typical for Ubuntu desktops but may not work correctly if user has multiple audio sinks and modifies a non-primary one
